task.description: WF-02 Step 3 test design for REQ-032 (no-show reason capture), the final requirement of Release 1, on branch feature/WF02-REQ-032, after REVIEWER and SECURITY-REVIEWER both PASSED. Scope test: Step 2 produced real behavioral surface (new scheduler job, new handlers, extended domain functions, real DB writes) -- full Steps 3b/4 apply, not the docs-only skip path.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: after ends_at, an admitted+never-checked-in registration receives exactly one message offering the five fixed reasons plus a free-text option; a checked-in registration receives nothing.
AC2: selecting a reason writes it to registrations.no_show_reason, verified by reading the row back (both the fixed-reason path and the free-text 'other' path).
AC3: re-running the job at T+24h and T+48h delivers NO further message to the same registration, counted across all runs (zero additional sends, not REQ-031's 'exactly one reminder').
AC4: no boolean no_show column exists in any migration and no job writes one.
AC5: the no_show derivation returns exactly one no-show for a constructed admitted-checked-in / admitted-not-checked-in / withdrawn triple, evaluated after ends_at.
AC6: the message reaches a user with broadcast_opt_in=false (transactional).
AC7: the handoff result (step-02-backend-dev.json) records that the no-show wording is provisional pending the product owner.
S3 exploit case: a forged/leaked registrationId across all three noShow.ts entry points (fixed-reason callback, 'other' callback, free-text reply) is refused with no write.

result.summary: Wrote docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-032.md mapping all 7 acceptance criteria plus the S3 exploit case to precise, runnable automated vitest test cases (no manual-checklist language -- this project has a real vitest suite for apps/bot, per REQ-031's own precedent). Two new DB-backed vitest files are specified: apps/bot/src/scheduler/noShowJobs.db.test.ts (job-level: AC1+AC6 in one fixture -- sent.length===1 with B excluded by checked_in_at IS NULL, a 6-button keyboard in NO_SHOW_REASON_CODES order plus 'other', broadcastOptIn=false piggyback; AC3 across 4 runs -- T0 send, immediate re-run at T0 proving ledger-UNIQUE dedup, T+24h and T+48h re-runs proving the CATCH_UP_WINDOW_MS(2h) window itself excludes the candidate, both mechanisms exercised independently per the design's own §2/§3.2 reasoning) and apps/bot/src/handlers/noShow.db.test.ts (dispatch-level, real grammY Bot + bot.handleUpdate() + bot.api.config.use() capture, mirroring handlers/feedback.db.test.ts's established shape: AC2 sub-case A -- fixed-reason button write + a re-tap gate proving no second write; AC2 sub-case B -- the free-text 'other' path writing the raw TRIMMED text, distinguished from a fixed-reason-code write; S3 exploit -- 3 attacks, one per entry point, each independently asserting show_alert:true/notYours + zero DB write + (for the reply-forgery attack) a legitimate same-prompt reply from the real owner succeeding immediately after, proving the refusal was identity-specific not a broken handler). AC4 is specified as a static git grep of apps/bot/drizzle/*.sql plus the new source files, confirming the only no_show-prefixed identifier anywhere is no_show_reason itself (verified this holds today: git grep -in no_show -- apps/bot/drizzle/*.sql returns exactly one line, 0001_tired_annihilus.sql:58). AC5 is specified as 3 new describe/it cases added to the EXISTING plain (no-DB) apps/bot/src/domain/registration.test.ts, calling isNoShow(...) directly with the three constructed AdmissionState/checkedInAt/endsAt combinations from a fixed evaluationTime strictly after endsAt -- chosen over a DB-backed test because AC5's own wording names the derivation itself, and registration.test.ts is this file's own established convention for testing its other pure functions (decideRegistrationOutcome, generateQrToken) without DB indirection. AC7 is specified as a direct read of handoffs/WF02-REQ-032/step-02-backend-dev.json's result.issues array, confirming the MAJOR-severity provisional-wording disclosure is present -- I independently verified this entry already exists in the committed handoff (read the file directly, quoted its exact opening text in the spec) rather than assuming BACKEND-DEV's own summary. This verification method exactly mirrors docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-014.md's own AC4 precedent for the identical situation (a process/handoff requirement with no runtime surface) -- the spec states this rationale explicitly (AC7's own section) rather than silently picking a mechanism, since AC7 is a genuinely different shape of check from the other 6 (a documentation-content read, not a dispatched-update assertion), and the spec calls this out so TEST-RUNNER/TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR know why no vitest it() exists for it. Every case names the exact fixture, exact evaluationTime (with the window arithmetic worked out numerically against noShowJobs.ts's actual CATCH_UP_WINDOW_MS=2*60*60*1000 constant, read directly from the source file, not assumed), exact expected DB state/captured-message content, and a named failure mode it would independently catch -- no case exists solely to satisfy the gate without a real regression it would fail against. tg_id ranges claimed: apps/bot/src/scheduler/noShowJobs.db.test.ts at 995_000_000+, apps/bot/src/handlers/noShow.db.test.ts at 996_000_000+ -- confirmed via a fresh grep -rn "nextTgId = " apps/bot/src (18 existing declarations found, highest non-notification.test.ts value is feedback.db.test.ts's 994_000_000; notification.test.ts uses 1_000_000_900) -- both claimed ranges are clearly beyond REQ-031's 993_000_000/994_000_000 and clearly below notification.test.ts's 1_000_000_900, with a 1,000,000-wide gap on each side, no collision with any of the 18 existing ranges.
